title: Dansgaard-Oeschger events
summary: Dansgaard-Oeschger events are abrupt warmings of the Last Glacial recorded in Greenland ice cores, where oxygen-isotope profiles swing between cold stadial and milder interstadial phases. NorthGRIP data for the glacial inception, about 123 to 100 thousand years ago, show warmings of 10 ± 2.5 and 16 ± 2.5 degrees C for events 23 and 24. The events are commonly linked to changes in Atlantic overturning circulation.

uncertainty.note: The range is only the glacial-inception window of the NorthGRIP study (~123-100 kyears BP, events 25, 24 and 23); Capron et al. (2021) study abrupt warming transitions down to 112 ka b2k and describe D-O events as recurring through the Last Glacial, so the full process is longer than this range. The id says 115 ka. ka values are used as stated with no 1950 offset.
